newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Gunmen kill Philippine journalist, injure wife.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kill Philippine journalist, injure wife.

text.p: Gunmen shot and killed a veteran Filipino journalist and wounded his wife outside their home just north of Manila, police said on Monday.

Alberto Berbon, the second senior journalist to be shot and killed in the Philippines this year, was chatting with relatives outside his home in the town of Imus on Sunday evening when he was attacked, police said.
They said the two gunmen got out of a car and fired at Berbon with an assault rifle and a pistol. A bullet struck his wife but her injuries were minor, they said.
Berbon, 45, was a senior editor at DZMM radio station, a part of ABS-CBN Broadcasting Corp, which owns the country's biggest television station.
Press and citizens groups condemned the killing.
"The National Press Club of the Philippines (NPC) strongly condemns the brutal slaying of...Berbon," club president Fred Lobo said in a statement.
"The shooting of Berbon outside his own home is a tragic blow to press freedom and an insult to our civilised society," Lobo said, urging the government to arrest and punish the attackers.

"If a radio reporter of the calibre of Mr Bert Berbon could be killed in Mafia fashion, then it would not be difficult to comprehend that an ordinary Filipino citizen could be killed any time by people who wish them harm," the anti-crime citizens watchdog Crusade Against Violence (CAV) said.
The killing of weekly Press Freedom editor Ferdinand Reyes by a lone gunman in southern Dipolog city last February has not been solved.
More than 50 journalists have been killed in the Philippines in the past 20 years, many of them during the martial law regime of late president Ferdinand Marcos.
